Model split:
- NER/Mentions: NuExtract-2.0-8B (purpose-built extractor, highest F1 on NER benchmarks)
- Assertions/SPO: Gemma 4 27B (best open-source for structured reasoning)
- Embeddings: nomic-embed-text (unchanged)

Prompt improvements (from LLMStructBench P-Strategy):
- Include JSON schema explicitly in system prompt
- Provide concrete input→output examples (few-shot)
- Keep schemas flat (depth ≤3)
- Focus on value accuracy not schema compliance
- Add congress-specific entity type guidance with examples
- Add SPO direction examples (Sponsor→sponsors→Bill, NOT Bill→was sponsored by→Bill)

Post-processing:
- Deduplicate mentions by span
- Filter self-referential assertions (subject == object)
- Normalize predicate direction
- Filter immaterial assertions (confidence < 0.7)

Applies to both congress-data AND media-ingest pipelines.

title: 5 killer validation Cypher queries as test suite
description:
Implement and validate all 5 killer queries against the Neo4j graph as a pytest test suite. Each query must return results (non-empty) against a seeded test graph or the live 119th Congress data.

1. Bipartisan bills that stalled in committee — needs COSPONSORED edges with party (via MEMBER_OF temporal), Action nodes with no floor-action terminal
2. Members whose floor votes diverge from cosponsorship — needs VOTED edges + COSPONSORED on same Member-Bill pair (depends on CD-jdc vote ingest)
3. Amendments by freshmen to climate bills — needs Term (first term = terms_served=1), PolicyArea, SPONSORED_AMENDMENT edges
4. Text drift introduced→enacted — needs BillVersion chain (ih→enr), PublicLaw terminal
5. LLM mentions of senator not in structured sponsors — needs Mention→EntityCandidate→CanonicalEntity→Person→Member traversal vs SPONSORED/COSPONSORED edges

Each query must be a parameterized Cypher function callable from the API or notebooks.

Add 'device' and 'model' labels to the histogram declaration, and plumb through at transcription.py:231 where .observe(rtf) is called. For the openvino path, device comes from config.openvino_device (resolved actual, not requested — if GPU fallback happened, use 'CPU'). For faster-whisper, device comes from config.whisper_compute_type or 'cpu'. Both bugs fit one small PR.

title: Smart section-based chunking for congressional bill text
description:
Current chunking splits bill text by character count (2000/200) which cuts mid-section and loses context. Congressional bills have well-defined structure that should be respected:

- SECTION N. TITLE (top-level sections)
- (a) Subsection headers
- (1), (2) Clauses
- ``(quoted amendments)
- TITLE / CHAPTER / PART markers
- Preamble (enacting clause, committee referral)

Proposed approach: parse bill text into structural sections first, then chunk within sections if they exceed max_size. Each chunk carries section metadata (section number, title, parent section). This gives the LLM full context for NER/assertion extraction — knowing 'this is Section 3(b)(1) of the Rural Housing Act' is critical for understanding what's being regulated.

Also consider: the GPO Formatted XML has explicit section tags (<section>, <subsection>, <paragraph>) which would be even cleaner than parsing plain text. Could parse XML instead of stripping to plain text.
design:
1. Add congress_data.chunking module with section-aware splitter
2. Parse bill text for SEC./SECTION/TITLE markers
3. Split into sections, carry section_id + section_title as chunk metadata
4. Fall back to character-based chunking for sections that exceed 4000 chars
5. Keep preamble (header, enacting clause) as its own chunk
6. Alternative: parse Formatted XML from congress.gov instead of HTM

Each Dockerfile has a brittle manual list:
```dockerfile
COPY libs/catalyst-contracts-core/ /tmp/catalyst-contracts-core/
COPY libs/catalyst-llm-contract-mcp/ /tmp/catalyst-llm-contract-mcp/
COPY libs/catalyst-langgraph-aio/ /tmp/catalyst-langgraph-aio/
COPY libs/dagster-io/ /tmp/dagster-io/
RUN uv pip install /tmp/catalyst-contracts-core/ && ...
```
Adding a new lib or a new cross-lib dependency requires editing every Dockerfile that transitively needs it. This just caused a production outage (media_mentions + media_assertions failing with ModuleNotFoundError).

## Desired state
Shared libs declare their dependencies on each other in pyproject.toml, and each package's pyproject.toml declares which shared libs it needs. The Dockerfile installs the package and its deps resolve automatically.

## Options to evaluate

### Option A: Workspace-relative path dependencies in pyproject.toml
```toml
# dagster-io/pyproject.toml
dependencies = ['catalyst-contracts-core']

# media-ingest/pyproject.toml  
dependencies = ['dagster-io', 'catalyst-llm-contract-mcp', 'catalyst-langgraph-aio']
```
Dockerfile just installs the package and uv resolves the tree. Requires all libs COPY'd before install but the dependency graph is explicit.

### Option B: Single COPY + install-all-libs step
```dockerfile
COPY libs/ /tmp/libs/
RUN uv pip install /tmp/libs/catalyst-contracts-core/ /tmp/libs/catalyst-llm-contract-mcp/ /tmp/libs/catalyst-langgraph-aio/ /tmp/libs/dagster-io/
```
Simpler but busts Docker cache whenever ANY lib changes.

### Option C: Publish libs to a private PyPI (or GHCR OCI)
Libs get versioned and published. Dockerfiles just pip install them by name. Clean separation but adds CI complexity.

## Recommendation
Option A is the sweet spot — explicit deps in pyproject.toml, automatic resolution, no external registry needed. uv handles workspace path deps natively.
design: Whatever we pick must: (1) make it impossible to forget a transitive dep, (2) not break Docker layer caching for code-only changes, (3) work with uv in the Dockerfile.

title: Add Mac M3 as complementary Dagster runner node for transcription/diarization
description:
Add Apple Silicon (M3) as a THIRD GPU compute target alongside the existing Intel Arc nodes (talos02-gpu + talos06). All three nodes run transcription/diarization in parallel — Dagster schedules to whichever has capacity.

## Current GPU topology
- talos02-gpu: Intel Arc, 4x i915 devices
- talos06: Intel Arc 140T, 4x i915 devices
- mac-node (planned): Apple M3, Metal GPU

## Why
- Apple Silicon Metal gives 10x+ realtime on whisper large-v3
- Triples GPU capacity — 3 nodes can transcribe different partitions simultaneously
- No single point of failure for GPU workloads

## Architecture
Dagster → K8sRunLauncher → step pod scheduled to ANY GPU node:
  - talos02-gpu (Intel Arc): OpenVINO whisper + torch.xpu pyannote (existing, unchanged)
  - talos06 (Intel Arc 140T): same Intel path (existing, unchanged)
  - mac-node (M3): mlx-whisper + MPS pyannote (new)

## Implementation steps

### 1. Multi-arch Docker image for media-ingest
- Add linux/arm64 build target (media-ingest currently AMD64 only)
- ARM64 variant installs mlx-whisper instead of OpenVINO (build arg or separate stage)
- AMD64 variant unchanged — keeps OpenVINO + torch XPU
- pyannote: verify MPS backend works on ARM64 for diarization

### 2. New whisper backend: mlx-whisper (ARM64 only)
- Add 'mlx' backend option to MediaIngestConfig.whisper_backend
- Implement _load_mlx_whisper() and _transcribe_mlx() in transcription.py
- Same output format as existing backends (segments, words, language)
- Backend selection via WHISPER_BACKEND env var per node

### 3. Node scheduling — soft affinity, not hard requirement
- Node labels: gpu-type=intel-arc (talos02, talos06), gpu-type=apple-metal (mac-node)
- Do NOT change Intel path — gpu.intel.com/i915 request stays as-is
- Mac node uses different resource request (no i915, generic label)
- Dagster schedules to whichever node has capacity

### 4. Config-driven backend per node
- WHISPER_BACKEND=openvino on Intel nodes (default, unchanged)
- WHISPER_BACKEND=mlx on Mac node

### 5. Liqo/OrbStack prerequisites (talos-homelab repo)
- OrbStack k3s on Mac with Liqo peering to Talos cluster
- NFS mounts for media files and model cache
- Node labels and GHCR pull secret

## What does NOT change
- Intel Arc transcription path (OpenVINO) on talos02-gpu and talos06 — untouched
- Intel Arc diarization path (torch.xpu) — untouched
- Transcoding stays on Intel Arc (QSV hardware encoder)
- All downstream assets (chunks, mentions, etc.) are hardware-agnostic

title: Node-local model cache for whisper/pyannote (avoid NFS load per step pod)
description:
Every transcription/diarization/speaker_embeddings step pod loads models from NFS (/data/whisper-models on TrueNAS). This is 2-3GB over the network on every pod startup. Models rarely change — cache them on node-local storage.

## Current state
- WHISPER_MODEL_CACHE = /data/whisper-models (NFS PVC from TrueNAS)
- OpenVINO whisper model: ~1.5GB, loaded by media_transcriptions
- pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1: ~1.5GB, loaded by media_diarization
- pyannote/embedding: ~200MB, loaded by media_speaker_embeddings
- Each step pod mounts NFS and reads the full model on every run

## Proposed fix
1. Add a hostPath or local-path PVC mounted at /cache/whisper-models on GPU nodes
2. In model load functions, check local cache first, copy from NFS if missing
3. Cache persists across pod restarts on the same node (survives pod churn)
4. NFS mount remains as the authoritative source for model updates

## Alternative: emptyDir with init container
- Init container copies from NFS → emptyDir on pod start
- Faster than NFS reads during model.load() but still copies every pod startup
- Only wins if sequential copy is faster than random-read model loading

## Measurement needed
- Profile MODEL_LOAD_DURATION metric to see how much time is NFS vs actual model init
- Compare NFS load time vs local SSD load time for the whisper model

title: Platinum: add speaker_profile signal to CrossSourceAligner + tag EntityCandidates with profile_id
description:
Follow-up from CD-40b spike. Design doc: docs/concordance/speaker-id-spike.md. Depends on CD-34j.1 (ingestion-side speaker profiles) and benefits from CD-0sc (intra-source alignment).

# What

Wire the `profile_id` from `media_speaker_profiles` through to `CrossSourceAligner` as a new alignment signal, so two `EntityCandidate`s that share a speaker profile merge into a single canonical entity.

# Why

CD-40b identified speaker identity as a strictly stronger signal than name matching — if the same voice shows up in two transcripts, that is acoustic evidence of same-person even when names differ, are paraphrased ("the president"), or are absent entirely. The ingestion side (CD-34j.1) produces stable `profile_id`s; this task makes the platinum aligner consume them.

# How — implementation notes

## Step 1: tag EntityCandidates with profile_id

In packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/assets/entity_candidates.py (or wherever mentions get built from the diarized transcript — confirm the exact file), for any Mention whose timestamp range falls inside a speaker turn, attach the `profile_id` of that turn's speaker. Extend `EntityCandidate` (libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/models.py) with an optional `profile_id: str | None = None` field. When the concordance engine resolves mentions, the candidate carries forward the dominant profile_id of its member mentions (majority vote).

Additionally, emit a new `mention_type=SPEAKER` candidate per profile_id so "the person speaking in this segment" becomes a first-class entity even when no name is uttered.

## Step 2: add speaker_profile signal to _score_pair

In libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/concordance.py:290-324, add a 5th signal block alongside exact_name/substring/jaccard/embedding:

```python
# Signal 5: Speaker profile match
if a.profile_id and b.profile_id and a.profile_id == b.profile_id:
    signals.append((0.92, "speaker_profile"))
```

Weight 0.92 sits just under exact_name (0.95) but above substring (0.80). Rationale from spike doc §3: speaker profile is a strong same-person signal but still noisier than an exact string match on a well-known name.

This must compose with existing signals under the current `max + 0.05 * (n-1)` combined-score rule at concordance.py:329-332.

## Step 3: feature flag

Gate the new signal behind `SPEAKER_PROFILE_ENABLED` env var so deployment can roll back without breaking CrossSourceAligner. When disabled, `profile_id` is ignored and the aligner behaves as today.

## Step 4: intra-source composition

title: Ingestion: media_speaker_embeddings + media_speaker_profiles assets with pgvector persistence
description:
Follow-up from CD-40b spike. Design doc: docs/concordance/speaker-id-spike.md.

# What

Add two new gold-layer assets in media_ingest that produce stable cross-file speaker identities from pyannote embeddings, persisted to pgvector in postgres_knowledge.

1. `media_speaker_embeddings` — partitioned by document_id (same partition as media_diarization). For each SPEAKER_XX emitted by the pyannote pipeline, compute the centroid embedding by running pyannote/embedding (`PretrainedSpeakerEmbedding`, 192-d) over the speaker's segments and mean-pooling. Output schema per partition: list of `{partition_key, local_label, centroid[192], segment_count, total_duration_s, avg_quality}`. Filter out segments shorter than 3s (noisy).

2. `media_speaker_profiles` — unpartitioned, consumes `media_speaker_embeddings` via `AllPartitionMapping()` fan-in (same pattern as canonical_entities at packages/knowledge-graph/src/knowledge_graph/assets/canonical_entities.py:71-74). Runs sticky agglomerative clustering: for each new centroid, compute nearest-neighbor cosine distance against existing `speaker_profiles` rows via pgvector; if < 0.25 merge into that profile, else seed a new one. Emit one `SpeakerProfile` per cluster and dual-write to pgvector + return as asset output.

# Why

CD-40b spike diagnosed that pyannote's SPEAKER_XX labels are file-local — voice-A in video 1 and voice-A in video 2 get different labels. This asset pair produces a stable `profile_id` per real-world speaker across the corpus, which becomes the v1 input to cross-document concordance (follow-up task for the platinum integration).

# How — implementation notes

- Embedding extraction should piggyback on the pyannote pipeline load already happening in packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/assets/diarization.py:84-114. Do not load a second model. If the diarization `Pipeline` doesn't expose segment embeddings directly, instantiate `PretrainedSpeakerEmbedding("pyannote/embedding", ...)` once per asset run and reuse across segments.
- Coordinate with CD-q8t (XPU diarization) — if that lands first, compute embeddings on the same GPU pass to avoid a second audio read from NFS.
- pgvector schema from spike doc §5:
  ```
  CREATE TABLE speaker_profiles (
    profile_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    centroid vector(192) NOT NULL,
    display_name TEXT,
    member_count INT, total_duration_s REAL,
    first_seen TIMESTAMPTZ, last_seen TIMESTAMPTZ
  );
  CREATE INDEX ON speaker_profiles USING ivfflat (centroid vector_cosine_ops);
  CREATE TABLE speaker_profile_members (
    profile_id, document_id, local_label, segment_count, PRIMARY KEY(...)
  );
  ```
  Add migration in packages/knowledge-graph/migrations (same location canonical_entities uses).
- `profile_id = sha1(centroid_bytes + first_seen_iso)[:16]`
- Persistence layer hooks into knowledge_graph/resources.py GraphDBResource — add `upsert_speaker_profile(profile)` and `find_nearest_profile(centroid, threshold)` methods.
- Gate everything behind `SPEAKER_PROFILE_ENABLED` env flag (default off) so media_ingest keeps working during rollout.

# Acceptance criteria

- Both assets exist and materialize without errors on the test media_ingest partitions.
- `speaker_profiles` table populates after first run, with pgvector index present.
- Sticky clustering verified: running the asset twice on the same partitions produces the same `profile_id`s (IDs do not drift).
- A manual test with 2 videos containing the same known speaker produces ≥1 merged profile, not 2 singletons.
- Metrics: `SPEAKER_PROFILE_TOTAL` gauge, `SPEAKER_PROFILE_MERGE_DISTANCE` histogram for threshold calibration (spike doc §6 risk 4).
- No regression in media_diarization runtime (embedding extraction adds < 30% over current diarization wall clock).

# Risks from spike doc §6

- Low-SNR audio quality — log avg-quality per profile, flag < 0.5 for review.
- Voice overlap — accept as v1 noise, don't filter aggressively.
- Threshold calibration — 0.25 is a starting point, expose as asset config.

title: Spike: speaker ID / voice profiling as intra-doc + cross-file concordance mechanism
description:
# What

Research and design a speaker identification / voice profiling layer for media-ingest that produces stable, cross-file speaker identities (not just pyannote's anonymous SPEAKER_XX labels). The resulting identity labels become a first-class entity-resolution signal at the platinum layer — specifically, they enable intra-doc and cross-document concordance that the current CrossSourceAligner cannot produce.

# Why this matters (the gap we just diagnosed)

During the April 11 recovery session, run 3f58561a (canonical_entities on 15 media partitions) produced:
- source_candidates = 1514
- canonical_entity_count = 1320
- alignment_edges = 0

The 0 alignment edges is structural, not a bug. CrossSourceAligner.align() at libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/concordance.py:249-279 only emits edges ACROSS different source keys (for i in locations: for j in locations[i+1:]). With only media_ingest feeding the platinum layer, there are no cross-source pairs, so every candidate becomes its own singleton canonical. Resolved in name, consolidated in zero ways.

The per-document concordance that media-ingest already does via ConcordanceEngine.resolve() at concordance.py:77-225 (exact/substring/jaccard/embedding passes over EntityCandidates WITHIN a single document partition) handles intra-doc dedup — but it cannot merge 'Joe Biden' across 15 distinct YouTube videos because each video runs in its own partition.

Two concordance gaps fall out of this:
1. **Intra-source cross-document resolution** — same named entity appearing in multiple documents within media_ingest (tracked as CD-0sc under the concordance epic)
2. **Speaker-level resolution** — transcripts currently emit SPEAKER_00, SPEAKER_01, etc. per pyannote diarization. Those labels reset per file. The same actual human voice in two videos gets two different SPEAKER_XX labels. There is currently NO mechanism in the pipeline to recognize that voice A from video 1 and voice B from video 2 are the same person.

Speaker ID at the ingestion layer attacks gap #2 head-on and is also a strong input signal for gap #1: if we know voice-profile-A appears as 'the president' in one transcript and 'Biden' in another, we have direct evidence the two name mentions refer to the same underlying entity — stronger than any string or embedding similarity.

# Current state to read

- packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/assets/diarization.py — pyannote speaker-diarization-3.1 runs per document. SPEAKER_XX labels are anonymous and file-local.
- libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/concordance.py:77-225 — ConcordanceEngine.resolve() is the existing per-document multi-pass concordance. Could potentially be extended or mirrored for voice clustering.
- libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/concordance.py:249-279 — CrossSourceAligner.align() is the platinum-layer consumer.
- packages/knowledge-graph/src/knowledge_graph/assets/canonical_entities.py — where speaker-identity signals would feed in.
- beads CD-0sc (P2, child of CD-34j) — sibling task for intra-source cross-document text resolution. The two should probably share a design doc.
- beads CD-q8t (P2) — existing XPU acceleration task for diarization. Speaker embedding generation may want to piggyback on the same GPU pipeline (embedding extraction is cheap if you're already running diarization).

# Research directions

- **pyannote embeddings** — pyannote.audio 3.x exposes speaker embeddings alongside diarization. Already in use, cheapest integration path. Per-segment embeddings could be averaged per SPEAKER_XX cluster and compared across files via cosine similarity.
- **ECAPA-TDNN** — speechbrain ECAPA-TDNN is the current SOTA open speaker embedding model for speaker verification. Higher quality than pyannote's built-ins, separate model load cost.
- **resemblyzer** — older but simpler, ~256d speaker embeddings, CPU-friendly.
- **WavLM-Base-Plus** — Microsoft's self-supervised speech model; used as a backbone for modern verification systems.
- Cross-file clustering approach: run all per-file SPEAKER_XX centroids through agglomerative clustering (threshold on cosine distance). Initial centroid population can be bootstrapped from an existing file, and new files either match existing clusters or seed new ones.
- Storage: pgvector or Neo4j vector index for the voice profile embeddings. pgvector is already in the stack (canonical_entities lives there).
- Manual naming UI: a Streamlit page in data-explorer where the user can attach a real name to a voice cluster once, which then propagates everywhere via the cluster ID.

# Design questions the spike should answer

1. Does this belong as a new gold-layer asset in media_ingest (e.g. media_speaker_profiles) or as a platinum-layer resolver alongside canonical_entities?
2. What's the data flow: per-file speaker embedding → per-file centroid → cross-file clustering → stable SpeakerIdentity entity → linkage back into EntityCandidate / CanonicalEntity?
3. How does the SpeakerIdentity signal feed CrossSourceAligner? Is it a new AlignmentSignal alongside exact_name/substring/jaccard/embedding in concordance.py:284-322, or a completely separate upstream that pre-merges candidates before alignment runs?
4. What's the minimum quality bar to ship a v1? A '2 centroids are the same speaker if cosine similarity > 0.8' heuristic could go live behind a feature flag without needing a UI for manual naming.
5. Is it worth sharing work with CD-0sc (text-based intra-source resolution) as one joint design doc or keeping them separate?

# Deliverable

A short design doc (committed somewhere under docs/ or beads --design) that answers the design questions above and proposes a concrete implementation plan: which assets to add or modify, which libs to depend on, which beads tasks to spawn for the actual implementation. No code in the spike — code lands in the follow-up tasks.

This is a spike, not a feature — output is a plan, not a feature. Success is 'we know what to build next and it's captured in a new beads task list'.
design: Likely technical decisions to pre-commit to: (1) start with pyannote built-in embeddings to minimize dependency churn and reuse the existing model load cost from diarization.py; (2) store voice profile vectors in postgres_knowledge pgvector alongside canonical_entities (same schema team, same query patterns); (3) first iteration produces only a cluster_id (no human name), manual naming is a follow-up; (4) the SpeakerIdentity type becomes a new input to CrossSourceAligner rather than a replacement, so existing text-based resolution continues to operate in parallel.

Design doc is reviewed against CD-0sc so the two tracks either merge or explicitly coexist.

title: Evaluate DB abstraction: ORM vs repository pattern vs SQLAlchemy Core
description:
Growing inline SQL across the codebase (21 execute() calls, 35 DDL statements in 2 Python files + k8s init). Need to pick an abstraction level before it gets worse.

## Current state
- annotation_store.py: 13 inline SQL statements (CRUD for annotations, speakers, entity overrides)
- resources.py (GraphDBResource): 8 inline SQL statements (canonical_entities, alignment_edges upserts + migrations)
- postgres-knowledge.yaml: 27 DDL statements (schema init, manual ALTER TABLE migrations)
- No migration tooling — schema changes are idempotent ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS

## Options to evaluate

### Option A: SQLModel (SQLAlchemy + Pydantic)
Full ORM where models serve as both DB schema and API types. Natural fit since we already have Pydantic models (EntityCandidate, CanonicalEntity, etc). But creates a second source of truth that may fight with Dagster's IO managers.
- Pro: Type safety, auto-migrations via Alembic, Pydantic integration
- Con: Heavy dependency, ORM overhead, dual source of truth with Dagster models

### Option B: Thin repository pattern (no new deps)
Keep raw SQL but centralize behind Repository classes with typed methods. Each table gets a class with .get(), .upsert(), .list() etc. Migrations stay manual.
- Pro: Zero new deps, minimal refactor, clear separation
- Con: Still raw SQL strings, no schema validation, manual migrations

### Option C: SQLAlchemy Core only (no ORM)
Table definitions + query builder without object mapping. Gets us schema management and parameterized queries without the full ORM overhead.
- Pro: Schema as code, query builder prevents SQL injection, Alembic for migrations
- Con: New dependency, learning curve, doesn't integrate with Pydantic models

## Research tasks
1. Check if Dagster has built-in patterns for this (dagster-postgres, dagster-sqlalchemy)
2. Evaluate SQLModel compatibility with Dagster's IO manager pattern
3. Prototype Option B on annotation_store.py to measure effort
4. Check if Alembic can coexist with the k8s init.sql pattern
design: Decision: pick ONE abstraction level. Do not mix patterns. Whatever we choose must work for both the viewer (FastAPI) and Dagster asset (step pod) contexts.

title: [bug] push_metrics() atexit noise — logger.warning races closed stderr during interpreter shutdown
description:
# What

During process shutdown (pytest cleanup, dagster step pod exit, etc), push_metrics() correctly swallows exceptions from push_to_gateway() but the subsequent logger.warning() call emits a cosmetic error:

    --- Logging error ---
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File ".../logging/__init__.py", line 1163, in emit
        stream.write(msg + self.terminator)
    ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.
    Call stack:
      File "libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/metrics.py", line 420, in push_metrics
        logger.warning("Failed to push metrics to pushgateway: %s", e)

# Why this matters

- Cosmetic only — the exception IS swallowed, metrics push failure does NOT propagate, and tests still pass (7/7 media-ingest test_definitions.py). Pre-existing from the OTLP era; CD-jsb preserved the pattern.
- But: it muddies test output and k8s step pod logs, making real errors harder to spot. If a CI run fails for an unrelated reason and the last 50 lines of log are this noise, debugging is harder.

# Root cause

atexit and SIGTERM handlers run AFTER Python has started tearing down its internal state, including closing sys.stderr. The stdlib logging module writes to stderr via a StreamHandler, and stream.write() on a closed stream raises ValueError. Python's logging module catches this internally and prints "--- Logging error ---" to whatever is left of stderr.

# Fix options

1. **Swap logger.warning for print(..., file=sys.__stderr__, flush=True)** inside the except clause — sys.__stderr__ is the original stderr, unaffected by shutdown-time redirection. Loses structured log format but we're shutting down anyway.
2. **Configure a NullHandler fallback** on the dagster_io logger so logger.warning becomes a no-op if the default handler's stream is closed. More invasive, affects all logging from this module.
3. **Detect interpreter shutdown** via `sys.is_finalizing()` and skip the log call entirely if true. Cleanest — the user doesn't see the log, but they also don't see the noise.
4. **Unregister the atexit handler after the first push** so we don't re-attempt on a broken stream. Doesn't help SIGTERM path.

Recommend option 3 (sys.is_finalizing check) combined with option 1 as a fallback for SIGTERM-but-not-atexit edge cases.

# Acceptance criteria

- pytest runs of libs/dagster-io/tests/test_metrics_push.py and packages/media-ingest/tests/test_definitions.py produce zero "--- Logging error ---" lines in output
- Dagster step pod logs in production similarly clean
- push_metrics() still swallows exceptions (no regression in atexit safety)
- New test: simulate closed stderr (monkeypatch sys.stderr with a closed StringIO) + trigger push failure, assert no exception AND no crash

# Related

- CD-jsb: introduced the fix path (push_to_gateway) but preserved the logger.warning noise
- libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/metrics.py:417-420
close_reason: Resolved by OTLP migration (CD-559) — pushgateway push_metrics() and atexit hooks removed entirely. OTLP uses PeriodicExportingMetricReader which shuts down cleanly.

title: Surface soft-failures in media_transcriptions / media_diarization
description:

Current behavior is intentional per-partition isolation (one bad file shouldn't wedge the whole pipeline), but it hides real errors behind '0 results' metrics.

Design decisions needed:
- Should we distinguish 'file is broken' vs 'transient failure' and fail runs for the latter?
- Add a dedicated ASSET_SOFT_FAILURE counter metric labeled by asset_key + reason?
- Mark the asset materialization with a distinctive tag (e.g. partial=true) so the Dagster UI surfaces it?
- Should downstream (chunks, mentions, etc.) explicitly check for upstream error flags and skip with a loud warning?

Not a blocker — pipeline works. But currently a single bad MP4 produces a chain of empty 'successful' materializations that looks identical to a healthy pipeline in dashboards.

title: media_transcriptions reloads full media_documents list per partition run

transcription.py:175 uses ins={'media_documents': AssetIn(partition_mapping=None)} which passes the entire unpartitioned media_documents list into every partition run, then filters with next(d for d in media_documents if d.id == partition_key).
